documents.t: SMSApp prepares SMS jobs in a web dashboard and dispatches them from your own Android phone through that phone's configured SIM. Anyone can sign in with Google and use the Free plan; Pro and Family raise the limits (plans). Supabase stores accounts, registered phones, synced contacts, jobs, recipients and results; it is not the SMS transport. First-release status The Android app com.aoneahsan.smsapp ("SMS Mobile App") is installed as a signed APK from the Apps page, not from Google Play. Updates to the app's web layer arrive inside the app. The web dashboard prepares and monitors jobs. The Android app runs on Supabase, the same backend as the web dashboard.

Install the Android app and sign in. Register the phone and explicitly enable it as a sender. Grant SMS permission and choose a default SMS subscription in Android. Grant contact access, then separately start cloud contact sync if contacts will be used. In the web admin, select that phone and choose synced contacts or a CSV file. Compose one message and review eligible, excluded, and duplicate numbers. Create the draft, assign it to the selected phone, and explicitly start dispatch. Keep the phone available and monitor per-recipient outcomes.

The first release accepts ordinary Pakistani mobile numbers in the 030–036 ranges. Local 03…, 923…, 00923…, and +923… forms may be normalized when their structure is unambiguous. The app excludes foreign numbers, landlines, short codes, service or premium destinations, malformed values, and unrecognized ranges. There is no override for excluded destinations. This filter reduces destination risk; it does not prove consent, current ownership, reachability, tariff, balance, or delivery. Send only to recipients who have agreed to receive the message. Carrier charges and limits still apply.

Item First-release behavior Sender One selected, owner-managed Android phone per job SIM One configured default SMS subscription Recipient sources Completed device contact sync or CSV Job size Up to 5,000 unique eligible numbers CSV size Up to 5 MiB Enrollment Explicit and off by default Incoming SMS Never read or uploaded Cloud gateway None Public device pool Not supported Dual-SIM selection Not supported in this milestone Delivery guarantee Not available; the app records the strongest Android result it can verify Long jobs can take many hours and may need owner attention after Android stops a foreground task, the app closes, the SIM changes, or connectivity is lost.

Bird runs SMS, email and WhatsApp on a funded balance. SMS Mobile App is SMS from your own SIM, to Pakistani numbers, on a plan.

documents.t: Your balance, rented numbers, inbox and other channels stay behind, and so does API access. Use up or withdraw the balance under Bird's own terms before you stop.

Put your list in a CSV file. Use whatever already holds the numbers, then follow Prepare a CSV recipient file. Check the numbers against what we accept. Only ordinary Pakistani mobile numbers in the 030–036 ranges go through. Everything else is refused with the reason, and there is no override. Install the app on the phone that will send. It is a signed APK, not a Google Play app: Install the Android app, and compare the SHA-256 before you open the file. Sign in and register that phone. Sign in with Google, register the phone, then grant its Android permissions. Create a small job first. Create a job from the CSV with a few numbers of your own, read the review screen, then release it. Watch what happens, then send the rest. Monitor the job. A SIM starts at 150 messages a day and at most 30 an hour, so plan a long list across days (limits).

Pakistani mobile numbers only. Foreign numbers, landlines and short codes are refused. Each SIM has daily and hourly caps. A SIM starts at 150 messages a day and can rise to 400 as delivery reports come back. Its hourly cap is a fifth of that, and a job waits at least 30 seconds between sends. The Free plan stops at 100 messages a month. No HTTP API. Other software cannot send through it, so OTP codes and automated sends from your own system are not available. Your SIM and carrier decide the rest. Whether a message arrives depends on them, and their SMS rate is yours to pay on top of any plan.

Architecture overview Why the sender is Android-only How Android SMS dispatch works Why SMSApp is not a default SMS handler Privacy and data handling SMS permission and Google Play The first release uses only owner-managed phones.

SMSApp separates job control from SMS transport. You sign in with Google, register your own Android phone, choose one recipient source, review a snapshot of the job and start it. Supabase (Postgres with row-level security) stores the account, phone, contact and job records. Your selected Android phone claims recipients and sends through its configured SIM.

The web dashboard gives a larger screen for import, review, assignment and monitoring. Supabase gives both surfaces one authenticated record. Every table has row-level security, and queue changes go only through database functions, so neither surface can skip a check. Android exposes SmsManager, the runtime SMS permission, a default subscription and sent-result callbacks. There is no SMS gateway. Every message leaves from a real phone's SIM.

The recipient policy runs during import, persistence, release and native dispatch. Contact data is scoped to the account and the phone it came from. Creating a job does not start it. One selected phone owns the job, and a claim lease stops another runner from silently taking the same recipient. Plan limits are checked by the database when a job is released. SMS outcomes are limited by what Android reports. A callback can confirm submission success or failure, but it cannot guarantee carrier delivery. A lost callback after modem handoff becomes uncertain and is never retried automatically.

The Android app com.aoneahsan.smsapp ("SMS Mobile App") is not released on Google Play. Google Play restricts SEND_SMS to a small set of approved uses, so the app ships as a signed APK from the Apps page and receives its web-layer updates inside the app. The Android app uses SEND_SMS for its core device-automation function, operated by the person who owns the phone, and does not request inbox or receive-SMS access.

After the owner explicitly starts a reviewed job, the Android foreground sender requests one eligible recipient at a time. It confirms assignment, job state, sender enrollment, SMS permission, and the configured default SMS subscription before calling Android's subscription-aware SmsManager. Android splits long messages into native SMS parts. SMSApp waits for sent callbacks and records success only when every part reports success. A known callback error becomes a failure. A timeout or interruption after modem handoff becomes uncertain because an automatic retry could duplicate the message. The sender spaces attempts according to configured pacing. Pacing does not guarantee carrier acceptance or make bulk traffic exempt from carrier or legal restrictions. Android may stop a long-running foreground task; the owner may need to reopen the app and resume safely pending work.

SMSApp has a narrow send-only role. It sends owner-approved outbound SMS through SmsManager, but it does not replace the phone's messaging app, read conversations, receive incoming SMS, or manage MMS/RCS threads. That boundary reduces data access and keeps the product's privacy model understandable. It also means SMSApp cannot inspect a recipient reply, verify inbox delivery, or provide conversation management. Those are unsupported rather than hidden features. The Android build requests SEND_SMS for dispatch. It does not request READ_SMS or RECEIVE_SMS and is not registered as the default SMS handler.
documents.s: Why SMSApp is not a default SMS handler

documents.t: SMSApp uses the authenticated owner identity, registered-phone state, selected contact names and phone values, batch message, normalized recipients, claim/result state, and operational timestamps needed to run the job. Contact sync is both permission-gated and owner-initiated. It stores the minimum name and phone fields required for recipient selection, scoped to the owner and source phone. A completed-generation marker prevents an interrupted replacement sync from appearing current.

SMSApp does not read or upload received SMS, call logs, location, advertising IDs, or legacy external-storage contents. It is not a default SMS handler. A public sender pool is not part of the first release.

Address-book presence does not prove consent. The owner must have an appropriate basis to send each message, honor opt-outs, protect account/device access, and follow carrier and legal requirements. Logs and analytics must not include message bodies, contact lists, or full phone numbers. The public app privacy policy governs the deployed service. This explanation must not be used as a substitute for that policy.

The sending surface depends on Android SmsManager, runtime SEND_SMS permission, a configured SMS subscription, and foreground-service behavior. The web browser can prepare and monitor jobs but cannot access a phone's modem or SIM. SMSApp therefore requires an Android phone for dispatch. There is no desktop sender or cloud SMS gateway in the first release. iOS: removed 2026-10-30 — re-add when an Apple Developer account exists. An operator may use the web admin from another device, but the selected registered Android phone performs every send. Android still controls permission prompts, foreground-task limits, SIM selection, and carrier interaction. SMSApp blocks when it cannot establish a safe default subscription rather than choosing another SIM silently.

Open the draft's detail screen and select one phone. For contact-based jobs, it must match the source phone. The phone must belong to the owner, be active, be explicitly opted in, have SMS permission, have a configured default SMS subscription, and support the current queue protocol. Confirm the assignment once. SMSApp creates a deterministic job for the batch and phone so repeated browser actions resolve to the same logical release rather than a second job. One job cannot fan out across multiple phones in the first release. Do not split a single authorized recipient snapshot across other devices.

Review accepted destinations, exclusions, duplicates, and segment estimates. Create the draft. Creation snapshots the message and recipients. It does not start dispatch. The contact source and sending device are the same phone for this milestone. The CSV path also requires a selected sending phone. The job is limited to 5,000 unique eligible ordinary Pakistani mobile destinations. Oversized, malformed, foreign, landline, service, short, premium, and unrecognized inputs are blocked.

documents.t: Open the Android app and confirm the signed-in account, active registration, explicit sender enrollment, SEND_SMS permission, configured default SMS subscription, and sender-service state. Keep the phone online long enough to publish readiness.

Correct the reported cause before using the retry action. Common causes include missing permission, missing default SIM, no carrier service, or a phone becoming unavailable before dispatch. The destination policy runs again and can block a previously staged value if policy changes.

Do not bulk retry. Android may have accepted the SMS before the app lost its callback or result upload. Check the phone and carrier records, then resolve the recipient explicitly. Treat duplicate-message risk as more important than making the progress counter look complete.

Android can stop a foreground task, the phone can reboot, or connectivity can disappear. Reopen SMSApp, restore readiness, and resume only the recipients that remain safely pending. Never replay the full source file as a new job without comparing existing outcomes.

Use the batch detail screen to review the selected phone, parent job state, recipient counts, and per-recipient outcomes. Refresh when needed; the Supabase database remains the durable coordination record. Outcome Meaning Pending Eligible and not yet claimed for dispatch Sending/claimed The selected phone holds the current lease Sent Android returned a successful sent callback Failed A confirmed failure was recorded Uncertain Dispatch may have occurred but the result cannot be proved Cancelled The job stopped before remaining recipients were dispatched “Sent” is not the same as carrier delivery. SMSApp does not read the inbox and does not promise a delivery receipt. Pause or cancel before changing device configuration. A pause prevents new modem calls after the phone observes it; it cannot recall a message already handed to Android.

Open SMSApp settings and enable the sender. Android prompts for SEND_SMS when needed. Approve it only on a phone you control and intend to use for dispatch. If denied or later removed, the phone must remain unavailable for jobs. SMSApp is send-only. It does not request permission to read or receive SMS and is not a default SMS handler.

Grant READ_CONTACTS only if you will create jobs from this phone's address book. Permission allows the app to read the address book locally; cloud sync still requires a separate Sync Contacts Now action. The sync sends only the name and phone fields required for recipient selection. Address-book presence does not establish consent to message a person.
Choose one default SMS subscription in Android settings. The first release blocks dispatch when no unambiguous default is configured. Per-job dual-SIM selection is not supported in this milestone.

Create a UTF-8 CSV no larger than 5 MiB. Include one recognized phone-number column. A header such as phone, mobile, phone_number, or phone number is accepted by the current importer. Duplicate or missing phone headers cause the import to fail. phone,name 03001234567,Example recipient +923061234567,Second example The message is composed in the admin and applies to the whole batch. A message column in the CSV is ignored. SMSApp normalizes unambiguous 03…, 923…, 00923…, and +923… forms, then keeps only ordinary Pakistani mobile ranges 030–036. It reports duplicates and rejects foreign numbers, landlines, short codes, service or premium numbers, malformed values, and unrecognized ranges. It never silently truncates more than 5,000 unique eligible recipients. Phone numbers must remain strings. Avoid spreadsheet scientific notation and formula cells. Review the accepted and excluded preview before creating the draft.

Install and open the verified Android APK. Sign in with the same owner account used in the web admin. Complete device registration and give the phone a recognizable name. Configure a default SMS subscription in Android. Grant SMS permission and explicitly enable the sender in SMSApp settings. Keep the app open until the web admin shows the device. New registrations are not enrolled to send by default. The admin should treat the phone as unavailable until it reports current SMS permission, a default SMS subscription, an active sender service, and the supported queue protocol. Registration does not share the phone with other accounts. The first release supports owner-managed phones only and one selected phone per job.

Open SMSApp on Android and choose Google sign-in. Select the project-authorized owner account. Open the web admin and sign in with the same account. Confirm that the account identity matches on both surfaces before registering or selecting a phone. Signing in authenticates the owner. It does not grant SMS permission, upload contacts, enable the sender, or start a job. If the two surfaces use different accounts, stop and sign out before creating data under the wrong owner.

Retry only when SMSApp records a confirmed pre-dispatch failure, such as readiness being revoked before the modem call. First correct the cause: restore connectivity, permission, the default SMS subscription, sender enrollment, or service state. Do not automatically retry an uncertain result. A timeout, app interruption, or lost callback after Android may have accepted the message can leave SMSApp unable to prove whether the recipient was already attempted. Check the handset and carrier state, then make an explicit reconciliation decision. Never retry excluded destinations. The Pakistani ordinary-mobile policy applies again at dispatch and has no override.

Confirm the Android phone is registered, explicitly enabled, and reports current SMS/default-SIM readiness. Open the admin batch import screen. Select that phone. Choose its completed contact sync or upload a CSV file. Enter one message. Review eligible, excluded, duplicate, and SMS-segment totals. Create the draft. Open the detail screen, assign the same phone, and explicitly start dispatch. Preparing a draft does not send SMS. The Android phone performs the sends only after launch. Keep the foreground sender available and expect long jobs to continue across sessions; at the default pacing, thousands of recipients can require days. Do not call an Android sent callback a delivery receipt. If SMSApp cannot prove whether a send occurred, it records an uncertain outcome for owner review instead of automatically retrying it.

SMSApp's records live in a Supabase Postgres database. Every table has row-level security. Record Responsibility devices The account's registered phones: active state, SMS permission, default SIM and readiness, and protocol version contacts · contact_phone_numbers Address-book entries from one phone, one row per number with the shared destination policy's verdict contact_syncs The last sync attempt per phone send_jobs One reviewed job: the message snapshot, the recipient source and the selected phone (a single message is a one-recipient job) send_job_recipients One eligible, normalized destination per job, with its claim lease and outcome send_attempts An append-only log of each modem attempt, with masked numbers plans The plan set and its limits, read by the database when a job is released Recipient destinations and message snapshots do not change after release. Claims use a lease on one selected phone, so another runner cannot silently own the same recipient. If the system cannot prove whether Android accepted a send, the recipient stays uncertain rather than becoming an automatic retry. This page leaves out field-by-field schemas. The released database migrations are authoritative.

Permission Purpose INTERNET, ACCESS_NETWORK_STATE Authenticate and synchronize phone, contact, job and result state with the Supabase database. SEND_SMS Send owner-authorized SMS through Android SmsManager. Granted at runtime. READ_CONTACTS Read names and phone values for an explicit device-scoped sync. Granted at runtime. FOREGROUND_SERVICE, FOREGROUND_SERVICE_DATA_SYNC Run the visible Android sender while work is active. POST_NOTIFICATIONS Show foreground/local notifications where Android requires runtime approval. RECEIVE_BOOT_COMPLETED, WAKE_LOCK Restore scheduling support and let bounded native work complete. VIBRATE Haptic feedback and notification behavior. SMSApp does not request inbox/read-SMS, receive-SMS, call-log, location, legacy external-storage, or advertising-ID access. It is not a default SMS handler. SMS permission and contact permission are independent. Granting contact access does not enable sending or upload contacts; granting SMS access does not start a job. Sender enrollment and cloud contact sync each require a separate owner action.

Each plan's limits are set on the plan by an admin and checked by the database when a job is released. The current values are on the pricing page. The importer rejects an oversized job instead of truncating it. These are product limits, not carrier allowances. A carrier may charge, throttle, block or prompt independently. A slow send rate on a large job means many hours of sending, so large jobs must survive several app sessions.

Row-level security and database functions in Supabase enforce these boundaries: Contact and sync records belong to the signed-in account and the phone they came from. A job's selected phone must belong to the same account, be active, and report SMS permission and a default SIM. Recipient destinations must match the normalized ordinary Pakistani mobile policy. Releasing, pausing and cancelling a job, claiming recipients and reporting results happen only through database functions, never as direct table writes. Message, destination, phone and source snapshots cannot be rewritten after release. The plan's limits (recipients per job, messages a month) are checked when a job is released. Admin access does not bypass destination safety. Phones on the same account share that account's sign-in. SMSApp checks the selected phone and the claim lease, but does not claim cryptographic per-phone identity isolation. Client validation improves feedback; the database checks and the native dispatch checks remain necessary because a modified client can bypass browser code.

Web dashboard -> sign in with Google -> select your phone and a recipient source -> normalize, exclude, deduplicate, preview -> create the job and its recipients as a draft -> explicitly release the job Supabase -> check the account, the phone and the plan limits -> persist phone, contact, job and recipient state -> hand out recipient claims (leased) and record results Android sender -> confirm the phone is ready: permission, default SIM, job state -> claim recipients -> enforce the destination policy again -> call subscription-aware SmsManager -> report a sent, failed or uncertain outcome Supabase is coordination storage, not an SMS gateway. The browser never dispatches a native SMS. The Android sender rechecks the job and its own readiness before each modem call and stops new attempts when state cannot be confirmed. Analytics and error-reporting events must exclude message bodies, contact data and full phone numbers. Operational state belongs in the authorized job records, not in public logs.

Follow these in order for the first owner-managed release: Get started with SMSApp Install the Android app Set up a contacts or CSV batch These tutorials do not cover a public sender pool, multiple sending phones per job, or dual-SIM selection because those are outside the current release target.
This walkthrough connects one owner-managed Android phone to the web admin. It does not send a real message until you explicitly start a reviewed job.

You need an Android phone with an active SMS-capable SIM, an APK from the owner's verified release channel, access to the SMSApp web admin, and a Google account authorized for the project. If you plan to run a real test, use a number you own and confirm your carrier tariff first.

Install the APK. Open SMSApp and sign in. Register the current Android phone. In Android settings, choose a default SMS subscription. In SMSApp settings, grant SEND_SMS and explicitly enable the sender. Enrollment starts off. Keep the app open while the first readiness update reaches the server. The admin should show the same phone and report whether SMS permission, default-SIM selection, protocol version, and sender service are ready. A recent sign-in alone does not mean the phone is ready to send.

Grant contact access on the phone. Separately choose Sync Contacts Now. Wait for the completed-sync timestamp. Contact permission does not start a cloud upload on its own. The completed generation contains the minimum name and phone fields needed for this workflow and remains scoped to the signed-in owner and source phone.

Open the web admin batch import screen. Select the registered phone. Select Synced contacts from phone or CSV file. Enter one SMS message. Review eligible, excluded, and duplicate totals. Create the draft and open its detail screen. Confirm the same phone as the only sender. Only ordinary Pakistani mobile destinations in the 030–036 ranges remain eligible. Excluded rows cannot be overridden.

Before a larger job, create a one-recipient batch using a safe number you own. Start dispatch once, keep the phone available, and check the recipient outcome in the batch detail. A sent callback means Android accepted the send attempt; it is not a guarantee that the carrier delivered the message. If the outcome is uncertain, stop. Reconcile the handset and carrier state before deciding whether another attempt is safe.
The Android app com.aoneahsan.smsapp ("SMS Mobile App") is installed as a signed APK from the Apps page, not from Google Play. Updates to the app's web layer arrive inside the app.

Download the APK from the Apps page. The page shows the current version and the file's SHA-256 checksum; compare the checksum with the file you downloaded before you install it. Do not use an APK from an unrelated website or message. The current executable application ID is com.aoneahsan.smsapp. A future package migration would require a separately signed installation and coordinated documentation update.

Open the verified APK on the Android phone. If Android blocks the install, allow installs from the specific app you used to open the file. Complete installation, then remove that temporary install permission if you do not need it. Open SMSApp and confirm that it reaches the sign-in screen. Android may refuse an update if the installed app was signed with a different key. Do not uninstall an existing copy until you understand what local state may be removed.
Continue with Get started with SMSApp. Registration, contact sync, and sender enrollment are separate steps; installation alone does not authorize SMS dispatch.

Open the admin batch import screen and select one phone owned by the signed-in account. The phone must be active, explicitly enabled, on the current sender protocol, granted SMS permission, and configured with a default SMS subscription. For contact-based jobs, the selected phone is also the contact source. SMSApp does not mix another phone's address book into this milestone.

Synced contacts: choose the latest completed sync from the selected phone. CSV: upload a UTF-8 CSV up to 5 MiB with a recognized phone column. The recipient policy normalizes eligible ordinary Pakistani mobile values and deduplicates the normalized results. It excludes all destinations outside 030–036, including foreign, landline, short, service, premium, malformed, and unrecognized values.

Enter one message for the batch. Review the message, SMS segment estimate, accepted recipients, duplicate count, and exclusion reasons. A batch may contain at most 5,000 unique eligible recipients; SMSApp rejects an oversized input instead of silently truncating it.

Create the draft, open its detail screen, and confirm the selected phone. Starting dispatch is a separate explicit action. Do not repeat the action while the browser is waiting; refresh the detail screen and verify whether the job already exists. Keep the Android sender enabled. Pause or cancel before changing SIM, permission, account, or phone configuration. An SMS already handed to Android cannot be recalled.
